title: TL-2000 Sting Sport: engine-mount crack, repair or replace

stages.name: Problem
stages.text: A crack was found at a joint of the steel-tube engine mount.

stages.name: Configuration
stages.text: TL-2000 Sting Sport, ROTAX 912. [OWNER CONFIRM: engine model; S-LSA or E-LSA]

stages.name: Evidence
stages.text: The crack was photographed in place before any work, to record its location and extent.

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.text: Repair and replacement were weighed. The repair path was taken to the aircraft designer instead of being decided on the shop floor. [OWNER CONFIRM: what repair instruction or data was used]

stages.name: Action
stages.text: The joint was weld-repaired. [OWNER CONFIRM: who performed the weld, if not LCA]

stages.name: Verification
stages.text: The repaired mount was inspected by magnetic-particle NDT at an outside testing facility. After the inspection, the aircraft designer confirmed in writing that the weldment is good and asked that the inspection protocol be added to the aircraft's documentation (correspondence shown with names and contact details redacted). Had the inspection not accepted the repair, the path was rework and re-test.

stages.name: Documentation
stages.text: The NDT report and the designer's confirmation are kept with the aircraft records. The mount was refinished before reinstallation.

limits: Repair data and acceptance are specific to this aircraft and this finding.

title: Sling 2 / ROTAX 912 iS: qualifying an E-PROPS propeller with the airframe manufacturer

stages.name: Problem
stages.text: An owner wants an E-PROPS propeller on a Sling 2 with a ROTAX 912 iS. The airframe manufacturer's position decides whether that is an approved configuration.

stages.name: Configuration
stages.text: Sling 2 (also relevant to the Sling LSA / NGT family), ROTAX 912 iS, applicable E-PROPS DURANDAL-3 configuration.

stages.name: Evidence
stages.text: An E-PROPS technical package with the propeller's configuration data and supporting type-certificate data. E-PROPS also supplied Sling-specific technical material and offered a propeller for testing.

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.text: Instead of treating one installation as automatically approved, we asked for a configuration-level review.

stages.name: Action
stages.text: Lima Charlie Aero submitted the package to Sling's technical, airworthiness and engineering staff.

stages.name: Verification
stages.text: Expected validation covers configuration, installation, weight and balance, pitch and RPM, vibration, performance, temperatures, fuel flow and a post-test inspection.

stages.name: Documentation
stages.text: The submittal and correspondence are kept. [OWNER DECIDE: publish package reference numbers? default no]

title: TL-2000 Sting Sport / ROTAX 912: E-PROPS qualification and installation verification

stages.name: Problem
stages.text: Fit an E-PROPS DURANDAL-3 to a specific TL-2000 / ROTAX 912 configuration with a controlled, documented process.

stages.name: Configuration
stages.text: Exact engine, gearbox and propeller configuration, with serialized components identified.

stages.name: Evidence
stages.text: E-PROPS application package. Mass, inertia, operating-limit and interface review. Vibration and torsional-compatibility background, including manufacturer test background.

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.text: The manufacturer authorization / LOA path was identified as a gate before installation was treated as settled.

stages.name: Action
stages.text: Installation to the planned criteria: pitch, tracking, torque and clearance checks. WOT/static-RPM target planning.

stages.name: Verification
stages.text: Dynamic balancing from recorded IPS, phase and RPM, with corrections toward a final balance target of about 0.07 IPS or less where applicable. Operational verification across the RPM range.

stages.name: Documentation
stages.text: Weight and balance, equipment list and maintenance-record updates.

title: Vashon Ranger R7: manufacturer-coordinated fuel evaluation

stages.name: Problem
stages.text: An owner asked whether a controlled-specification automotive gasoline could be used in a Vashon Ranger R7 with a Continental O-200-D.

stages.name: Configuration
stages.text: Client aircraft baseline, fuel-system architecture, engine limitations and the existing approval gaps.

stages.name: Evidence
stages.text: An 11-page engineering evaluation covering detonation and preignition margin, vapor lock and hot-fuel behaviour, wetted-material compatibility, fuel density and metering, contamination and misfueling controls, placards and POH implications, instrumentation, a risk register and go/no-go decision gates.

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.text: It treats two hazards separately: engine detonation suitability, and the installed aircraft's fuel-delivery and vapor margin. Passing one does not establish the other.

stages.name: Action
stages.text: The packet went to the aircraft owner and, at the same time, to the airframe and engine manufacturers' technical staff so they could evaluate the question together.

stages.name: Verification
stages.text: Manufacturer disposition pending. [OWNER CONFIRM]

stages.name: Documentation
stages.text: [OWNER CONFIRM]

title: SeaRey: return-to-service systems evaluation

stages.text: An amphibian returning to service after downtime: more than a routine annual or an engine-only check.

stages.name: Configuration
stages.text: SeaRey amphibian, ROTAX 912 UL.

stages.name: Evidence
stages.text: [OWNER CONFIRM]

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.text: The plan crossed system boundaries: ROTAX calendar items, hoses and rubber, carburetors, fuel pump, cooling, gearbox, compression and leak-down, fuel contamination, propeller, corrosion and downtime effects, wing-attachment hardware, amphibious-airframe systems, records and inspection status, and sale readiness. With the wings already off, the plan used the opportunity to inspect the attachment hardware and the surrounding structure.
